old: A system named for its creator got a new sound when it crossed the Channel — English readers pronounced the letters as they looked, not as the Frenchman said them.
It's named after a 19th-century French educator who was himself blind.
Say his surname the French way and it rhymes with 'eye,' not with 'day' — English chose the spelling over the sound.
clues: This system of writing carries the surname of the French educator who devised it, though English speakers pronounce his name differently from the way the French do.
It uses patterns of raised dots that blind people read with their fingertips. Unlike sign language, which is watched, this is felt.
You'll find it on elevator buttons and ATM keypads. In French, its inventor Louis's surname sounds closer to 'brye' than to the English 'brayl'.
